proposal_reason:
ANALYSIS: No fusion trials yet. The single-model+meta baselines are all close (0.862-0.870 AUROC), and the tuned members prefer very strong regularisation (C 1e-4 to 1e-3) with low-dimensional PCA. This suggests the per-model signal is low-rank and partly redundant, so fusion gains will likely come from averaging out variance rather than from new information.
REASONING: Start with the most robust fusion: late_tuned with mean_prob. Each member runs at its own validated setting, and equal-weight averaging has no extra parameters to overfit. This gives a clean reference point for whether combining the three models helps at all.
EXPECTED: Expect an AUROC of about 0.875-0.885, a little above the best single model (uni2h+meta, 0.870), because errors are partly decorrelated. If it comes out at or below 0.870, the models are largely redundant. Fusion would then need complementary per-class strengths, and learned weights or early_tuned would be the next things to test.

ANALYSIS: Late_tuned mean_prob reaches 0.8792 AUROC, about +0.009 over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.8701). That gain may sit near the acceptance threshold. Averaging probabilities helps most on Papillary and Lepidic, which are the weakest classes. Early, late, gated and early_tuned have not been tried yet.
REASONING: The exploration phase should map the methods. Early fusion with balanced blocks is the natural main competitor. PCA 32 per model, a moderate C of 0.001 and meta_weight 3 match the regime where the single models did best: heavy shrinkage on few components. Balancing the blocks stops Virchow2's 2560 dimensions from dominating.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.87-0.88. If it falls clearly below late_tuned, the conclusion is that concatenation overfits with 134 patients, and the search should focus on late-style ensembles. If it beats late_tuned, the next trials should explore early_tuned and C around this setting.

ANALYSIS: Both fusions so far (late_tuned mean_prob 0.879, early PCA32 balanced C=0.001 0.877) beat the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870) by about 0.008, which is near the noise threshold. The weak classes are Papillary (~0.78) and Lepidic (~0.83). Gated, early_tuned and late-with-stack are still untested.
REASONING: This is the exploration phase, so map the untested methods. early_tuned keeps each model's own tuned L2/PCA and learns block weights by inner CV, so it may combine the strengths of early and late fusion. C=0.001 matches the members' tuned strengths (0.0001-0.001), and meta_weight=3 is the middle value.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.875-0.885. If it is clearly below 0.877, per-block tuning inside one regression adds nothing over simple early fusion, and late averaging is the better route.

ANALYSIS: All three fusion families tried so far land at 0.876-0.879 AUROC, about 0.006-0.009 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). That gain is likely near the noise threshold. Papillary (0.76-0.78) and Lepidic (0.83) are the weak classes in every trial. The gated method and the late combiners other than mean_prob are still untested.
REASONING: The exploration phase should cover every method, and gated is completely unmapped. With only 134 training patients per fold, it needs a strongly regularised setup: PCA 32 per model, a small hidden size, high dropout and substantial weight decay. Running it now tells us whether learned per-patient gating adds anything over linear fusion.
EXPECTED: I expect roughly 0.86-0.875 AUROC, probably at or below the linear fusions because of overfitting. If it reaches about 0.88 or more, gated deserves tuning (hidden size, epochs). If it falls clearly below 0.87, I will drop gated and concentrate on late/late_tuned combiners such as stack and learned_weights, and on the C and PCA settings for early fusion.

ANALYSIS: All four fusion methods land at 0.873-0.879, roughly 0.005-0.01 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). That gain is around the noise threshold. late_tuned mean_prob leads. Early fusion with balanced blocks, PCA32 and strong shrinkage (C=0.001) is close behind. The gated network has the highest fold SD (0.040).
REASONING: This is still the exploration phase. The obvious untested axes are the learned combiners in late fusion: stack and learned_weights. A stacker can learn per-class reweighting across models. Papillary and Lepidic are the weak classes, and members may differ on them. Stacking with strong regularisation (stack_C=0.01) on the tuned members tests whether learned combination beats simple averaging without overfitting 134 patients.
EXPECTED: If stacking captures complementary per-class strengths, I expect AUROC around 0.88-0.89, with gains on Papillary and Lepidic. If it comes in below mean_prob (around 0.87 or lower), the inner-CV meta-learner is too noisy at this sample size. In that case simple averaging is the right combiner, and the remaining budget should go to early-fusion regularisation and preprocessing.

ANALYSIS: All simple fusions beat the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870) by about 0.005-0.009. late_tuned mean_prob leads at 0.879, with early balanced (0.877) and early_tuned (0.876) close behind. Stacking hurt (0.867), likely from inner-CV noise with 134 patients. Gated is competitive but noisier (SD 0.040). Papillary (~0.77) and Lepidic (~0.83) are the weak classes across all methods.
REASONING: Exploration should map the untested late knobs. A shared-setting late fusion with mean_logit and L2 normalisation at moderate PCA tests whether geometric averaging and a common, slightly less shrunk C behave differently from the tuned members. Late averaging has been the strongest family so far, so varying it is the most likely route to a clear gain. I use C=0.01 with PCA 32 to probe a weaker penalty than the tuned C of 0.001/0.0001.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.875-0.882. If it is clearly below 0.875, the shared weaker penalty hurts, and the tuned members with plain mean_prob remain the anchor. If it beats 0.879, I will explore the C/PCA neighbourhood of late fusion further.

ANALYSIS: All fusion methods cluster at 0.872-0.879, about 0.005-0.009 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Simple averaging (late_tuned mean_prob, 0.879) leads, and stacking hurts (0.867), which points to inner-CV weight learning being noisy at n=134. Early fusion with balanced blocks is competitive (0.877, best BA). Papillary (~0.77) and Lepidic (~0.83) are the weak classes.
REASONING: We are still exploring, so the space should be mapped further. Early fusion without PCA or L2 is untested, and neither is a stronger C. A key open question is whether early fusion with L2 norm and full dimensions at very low C (strong shrinkage, which suited the single models) beats PCA32. hoptimus1 liked L2 with no PCA. Testing l2=True, pca=None, balance_blocks=True, C=0.001 answers whether PCA is needed in early fusion.
EXPECTED: Expect AUROC around 0.875-0.885. If it is clearly lower than #2, PCA compression helps early fusion and later work should tune C and meta_weight around pca=32/16. If it is higher, full-dimensional L2 features with strong shrinkage are the better early-fusion base.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants cluster at 0.872-0.882, about 0.01 above the best single model (uni2h+meta, 0.870). Early fusion with L2, no PCA and balanced blocks at C=0.001 (#7, 0.8819) is the top so far, ahead of late_tuned mean_prob (#1, 0.8792). Stacking (#5) underperformed, probably because inner-CV predictions on ~134 patients are too noisy. Papillary (~0.77-0.79) and Lepidic (~0.83) remain the weakest classes across every method.
REASONING: The exploration phase should map regularisation strength around the current leader. C=0.001 with full-dimensional L2-normalised features (about 5600 columns) is strong shrinkage. I will test C=0.0001 in this trial; C=0.01 can be checked afterwards to locate the optimum. The tuned members preferred very small C (virchow2 at 1e-4), so stronger shrinkage of the concatenated block is plausible. Everything else stays as in #7 so the effect of C is isolated.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC between 0.875 and 0.885. If it beats #7, the optimum lies at stronger regularisation; if it drops clearly, I will try C=0.01 or a meta_weight change next. With the gap to single models at only ~0.01, any acceptance will likely need a configuration that lifts Papillary or Lepidic.

ANALYSIS: All fusion methods sit at 0.867-0.885 AUROC, a few points above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Early fusion with per-slide L2 normalisation, no PCA and balanced blocks is the strongest so far. Lowering C from 0.001 to 0.0001 helped (0.8819 → 0.8852) and also reduced the fold SD. Learned stacking hurt (0.867), so inner-CV-learned combiners look noisy at n=134. Late mean_prob with tuned members is decent at 0.879.
REASONING: Two exploration slots remain. The open question for the leading early-fusion recipe is whether metadata weight matters. Age and sex alone give only 0.60 AUROC, so meta_weight=10 might add signal or might add noise. Under strong shrinkage (C=0.0001) the metadata columns are heavily penalised, so a higher meta_weight is the knob most likely to move the score. An alternative was going below C=0.0001, but that value is the lowest allowed.
EXPECTED: If metadata carries complementary signal, I expect a small gain (about 0.003-0.008), driven by classes such as In situ and Lepidic that correlate with age. If AUROC drops or stays flat, I will conclude that metadata is already sufficiently weighted at 3, and keep meta_weight=3 for later refinements, such as trying balance_blocks=False.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with per-slide L2 norm, no PCA and block balancing is the strongest family. Stronger regularisation (C=1e-4) gave 0.8852 vs 0.8819 at C=1e-3, and meta_weight 3 vs 10 made no difference. Late_tuned mean_prob (0.879) is competitive, while stacking hurt, probably because inner CV leaves too little data. Gated did not beat simple linear fusion. Every fusion result is about 0.01 above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870), which is near the acceptance threshold.
REASONING: This is the last exploration slot. The remaining open question in the best family is whether balance_blocks matters. Without it, Virchow2's 2560 columns would dominate. Testing balance_blocks=False at the best setting (L2, no PCA, mw 3, C=1e-4) maps that knob. The other candidate, early_tuned with C=1e-4, matters less because early_tuned at 1e-3 was already weaker. Very small C already looks optimal, since it is the lowest grid value.
EXPECTED: I expect a slightly lower AUROC (about 0.880), which would confirm that block balancing helps or at least does no harm. If the unbalanced version matches or beats 0.885, block balancing is irrelevant and the gain comes from L2 plus strong shrinkage. In that case later trials should probe other levers, such as late_tuned with mean_logit or learned_weights, rather than block scaling.

proposal_reason:
ANALYSIS: Early fusion with per-slide L2, no PCA and very strong shrinkage (C=1e-4) is the best so far (0.8852, SD 0.026). It beats the best single model (uni2h+meta, 0.870) by about 0.015. Block balancing and meta_weight (3 vs 10) made no visible difference, and neither did lower C beyond small amounts. Late fusion was only tried with PCA and a moderate C (0.01). late_tuned mean_prob reached 0.879, while stacking hurt (0.867).
REASONING: The open question is whether the gain comes from the fusion structure or from the strongly regularised, full-dimensional L2 regime. Late fusion with mean_prob in exactly that regime (L2, no PCA, C=1e-4, meta 3) tests this directly. Averaging three heavily shrunk per-model classifiers adds ensemble variance reduction, which early fusion lacks. If the models' errors are partly independent, this could give a clear gain.
EXPECTED: Expect about 0.883-0.890. If it is clearly above #8, late averaging in the shrunk regime is the better path, and I would next try mean_logit or learned_weights there. If it is at or below #8, early concatenation already captures the complementarity. Further gains would then have to come from other structural changes rather than from changing the combiner.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with per-slide L2, no PCA and very strong shrinkage (C=1e-4) is best (0.8852, the lowest fold SD at 0.0255). This is about +0.015 over uni2h+meta. Stronger regularisation helped consistently (C 1e-3 → 1e-4). meta_weight 3 vs 10 and balance_blocks on or off made no detectable difference. Late, stacked and gated fusion all trail early fusion, and Papillary (~0.78) and Lepidic (~0.83) remain the weak classes.
REASONING: C is already at the bottom of its grid, so the remaining shrinkage-related lever in early fusion is PCA truncation. The question is whether discarding low-variance directions (PCA=128 per model, fitted in-fold after L2) helps beyond what ridge shrinkage already does. Earlier PCA trials used PCA=32 with C≥1e-3, which confounds PCA with weaker shrinkage. This trial isolates truncation at the best C and settles the last open early-fusion axis.
EXPECTED: Likely a similar AUROC (0.880-0.888), possibly with lower variance. If it is not accepted, I conclude that ridge at C=1e-4 already handles the high dimensionality, so the early-fusion family has plateaued. Remaining budget would then go to untested late_tuned combiners (learned_weights, mean_logit) and a more heavily regularised gated model.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion of the full-dimensional, L2-normalised blocks with the strongest shrinkage (C=1e-4) is best at 0.8852, and it beats every single-model baseline by about 0.015. Around that optimum, meta_weight (3 vs 10), balance_blocks and PCA128 make no difference. Late, stacked and gated fusion all trail. Lower C helped (0.8819 at 1e-3 vs 0.8852 at 1e-4), and C is now at the grid floor.
REASONING: One knob near the optimum is still untested: per-slide L2 normalisation at C=1e-4 with no PCA. Trial #2 (no L2) differs in both PCA and C, so the L2 effect is confounded there. This trial isolates L2 at the winning setting. That tells us whether L2 normalisation matters or whether the early-fusion region is simply flat at strong shrinkage. If it is flat, I can move the remaining budget to structurally different options such as late_tuned learned_weights or a more regularised gated model.
EXPECTED: I expect roughly 0.880-0.885, a tie or a small loss, which would confirm that L2 is mildly helpful or neutral and that the early-fusion optimum is flat. A clear gain above threshold would mean that raw-scale embeddings carry useful norm information under strong shrinkage. In that case I would explore meta_weight and balance_blocks again without L2.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with per-slide L2 normalisation, no PCA and very strong shrinkage (C=1e-4) is the best so far (#8, 0.8852, SD 0.026). Several knobs made no measurable difference: balance_blocks (#10), meta_weight 3 vs 10 (#9), L2 normalisation (#13) and PCA=128 vs none (#12) all came within ±0.001. Late, stacked and early_tuned variants are 0.004-0.018 lower. Gated reached 0.8725 with the highest fold SD, which is consistent with overfitting.
REASONING: The early-LR neighbourhood looks saturated, and C is already at the bottom of its grid, so more tweaks there would only chase noise. Gated fusion is the only method that differs in kind, because it can weight the models per patient. It has had only one trial, at moderate regularisation. The evidence favours L2-normalised inputs and heavy shrinkage, so I am testing gated in that regime: a small projection (hidden=16), maximum dropout (0.5), strongest weight decay (1.0), short training (100 epochs, lr=1e-3), PCA 32 to cut input dimension, and 3 seeds. This tells us whether gated was held back by overfitting.
EXPECTED: Fold SD should fall below #4's and AUROC should rise to about 0.878-0.888. If it stays below about 0.88, I will conclude that per-patient gating adds nothing on 134-patient folds. I would then deprioritise gated and spend the remaining trials on cheap checks: late_tuned learned_weights, early_tuned at C=1e-4, and early with PCA=16. I would stop early rather than chase sub-threshold differences.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion of full-dimensional, L2-normed, strongly regularized (C=1e-4) features is the plateau at ~0.885. It is insensitive to balance_blocks, L2, PCA 128 and meta_weight, all within ~0.001. Late, stack, gated and early_tuned variants are all worse. Papillary (~0.78) and Lepidic (~0.83) remain the weak classes. Untested late_tuned combiners are learned_weights, mean_logit and weighted_vote.
REASONING: Within early fusion, C is already at the lowest value in the grid, and the other knobs make no difference, so it is saturated. The main open question is whether learned_weights in late_tuned can beat the plain mean (0.879) by down-weighting weaker members. Each member there runs at its own tuned setting. That is a structurally different fusion, not a small knob tweak.
EXPECTED: Likely about 0.878-0.885. Acceptance would need roughly +0.005 over #8, which is unlikely but possible if the weighting helps the Papillary and Lepidic classes. If it fails, late fusion is dominated by early fusion. I would then try one or two early_tuned settings (C=0.0001 with meta_weight 10) before letting the stop rule end the search.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion of all three full-dimensional embeddings, with strong shrinkage, is the best so far: #8, 0.8852, with the lowest fold SD. It beats the best single model (uni2h+meta, 0.870) by about 0.015. Around #8 the early-fusion surface is flat: L2 on or off, block balancing, PCA 128 and meta_weight 3 or 10 all move AUROC by less than 0.001. Lowering C helped (0.001 to 0.0001 gave +0.003). Late, stacked, learned-weight and gated fusion all trail #8 by 0.008 to 0.016.
REASONING: #8 already uses the smallest C allowed, so early-fusion knobs are exhausted. The one remaining mechanism that could add signal is per-block weighting. Early_tuned was only tried at C=0.001 (0.8757), where it lost to plain early at the same C (0.8819). Re-testing it at C=0.0001 combines the strong-shrinkage regime that helped early fusion with inner-CV block weights, which can down-weight or drop a weaker model. This is the last untested combination with a plausible mechanism for a clear gain.
EXPECTED: Likely about 0.880 to 0.886, probably not clearing the ~0.002 to 0.005 threshold. If it fails, I conclude that per-block weighting and the members' own PCA settings add nothing beyond uniform strong shrinkage of the full embeddings. #8 is then near the ceiling for linear fusion, and the remaining trials should be spent sparingly or the search allowed to stop.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with per-slide L2, no PCA, balanced blocks and very strong shrinkage (C=1e-4) is best at 0.8852, beating the best single model (uni2h+meta, 0.870) by about 0.015. Near neighbours all land within ±0.001 and are rejected: meta 3 vs 10, balance on/off, L2 on/off, PCA 128 vs none, and early_tuned. Late, stacked, learned-weight and gated fusions are all clearly worse. The surface around the best is flat, and Papillary (about 0.78) and Lepidic (about 0.83) remain the weak classes.
REASONING: With C=1e-4, PCA 128 gave the same result as no PCA, so heavy ridge shrinkage already keeps mostly the top principal directions. The open question is whether a hard cut to very few components per model (16) acts as a different, stronger regulariser and helps. PCA 32 has only been tested at C=1e-3 without L2 (#2, 0.877). Testing PCA 16 under the winning settings isolates the dimensionality effect. Other directions look closed: late, stack, gated and learned weights are all below, and the meta and balance knobs are flat.
EXPECTED: Most likely a result within about ±0.005 of 0.885, which would be rejected and would confirm that the strong-shrinkage early-fusion optimum is reached. A clear gain above the threshold would mean hard truncation regularises better than ridge alone, and I would then try PCA 16/32 with a larger C. A clear drop would mean discriminative signal sits beyond the top 16 components, and I would stop exploring PCA.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with strong shrinkage (C=1e-4, full dimension) is the best at 0.885 (#8), clearly above the best single model (0.870). Variations in L2, balance_blocks, meta_weight, PCA 128 and early_tuned all land within ±0.001, so this is a flat plateau. Late, stacking, learned_weights and gated methods are all worse. The remaining open direction is the edge of the C grid: C=1e-4 is the smallest value allowed, and it beat 1e-3. Larger C has not been tested with full-dimension early fusion.
REASONING: Lower C cannot be tried, and the C=1e-3 to 1e-4 step gained only 0.003. So the plateau is probably reached at the low end. The untested region is late fusion over the full space with mean_logit at C=1e-4. That would likely tie as well. A more informative test is whether early_tuned with the highest meta_weight (10) helps: metadata weighting differed between members (virchow2 used 3, hoptimus1 used 10). Since #9 showed meta_weight=10 is neutral in early fusion, though, that would also likely be noise. Late mean_logit with the winning member settings (L2, no PCA, C=1e-4) answers whether geometric-mean pooling closes the gap with early fusion. mean_prob there lost 0.008 (#11). This is likely the last structurally different question worth one trial before accepting the plateau.
EXPECTED: Expect roughly 0.878–0.882, below #8 and rejected. That would confirm early concatenation at C=1e-4 is the best fusion found and that further trials only chase noise. If it unexpectedly beats #8 by more than the threshold, then logit-space averaging matters, and stack_C variants would be the next thing to explore.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion of L2-normalised full embeddings with strong shrinkage (C=1e-4) is on a plateau around 0.885 AUROC (#8, #9, #10, #12, #13, #16 are all within ±0.001). PCA, block balancing, meta_weight between 3 and 10, and L2 normalisation barely matter. Late, gated and learned-weight or stacked combinations are consistently 0.005–0.016 worse. Papillary (about 0.78) and Lepidic (about 0.83) remain the weak classes for every method.
REASONING: The early-fusion knobs are exhausted at the lower bound of C, so further early tweaks would only chase noise. The clearest untested arm is late_tuned with mean_logit. Its sibling, late_tuned mean_prob, was the best late variant at 0.879. A geometric mean of the per-model tuned members can sharpen agreement between models, which may help the confusable Papillary and Lepidic classes. This one trial closes the question of whether any late combination of the tuned members can rival early fusion.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.879–0.883, probably not accepted. If it falls short of #8 by more than the threshold, I will conclude that late fusion is dominated by joint early fusion here. The remaining budget would then go only to a few qualitatively different gated configurations before letting the stop rule end the search, with #8 as the final answer.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with strong shrinkage (C=1e-4, full dims, L2 or not, balance or not) sits on a flat plateau around 0.885, about +0.015 over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Every other method has scored below it: late, late_tuned, early_tuned and gated, with gated also the noisiest. Knob changes within early (meta_weight, PCA 128, L2, balance) all give differences of at most 0.001. C=1e-4 is the lowest grid value, and trial #7 shows C=1e-3 is worse.
REASONING: With 6 trials left before the stop rule, the plateau looks saturated, so spend a trial on the one untested axis with any plausible upside. Every early trial so far used meta_weight 3 or 10 at C=1e-4. Because C is so small, the metadata columns are heavily shrunk. Earlier evidence: meta_weight=10 at C=1e-4 gave 0.8845, the same as 3. The remaining open question is whether meta_weight=1 is worse, which would only confirm the current setting. A more informative alternative is late_tuned weighted_vote, the one combine rule not yet tested. However, mean_prob and mean_logit for late_tuned both scored about 0.88, below the best, so weighted_vote is unlikely to beat it. I prefer a gated configuration closer to the linear regime: PCA 16 with L2, hidden=64, low dropout, weight_decay 0.01, 100 epochs. It is the only family that could add nonlinear per-patient weighting, but evidence so far is negative. On balance, the most plausible gain is early with balance_blocks=False and L2 at meta_weight=10, but that differs from existing trials only trivially. Instead I test early without L2, unbalanced, at C=1e-4 and meta_weight=1, to check whether lighter metadata weighting changes Lepidic or Papillary.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.884 ± 0.002, which is not accepted. If so, early fusion is converged; I will try late_tuned weighted_vote, and if that fails as well I will let the search stop with #8 as the final fusion (+0.015 over the best single model).

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with L2 normalisation, no PCA and the strongest regularisation (C=1e-4) holds the best result at about 0.885. Its neighbours (meta_weight, balance_blocks, PCA 128, L2 off, early_tuned) all fall within ±0.001, so that region is flat. Late and late_tuned combiners (0.867-0.881) and gated runs with PCA 32 (0.871-0.873, high fold SD) are clearly worse. Every per-class AUROC is nearly identical across configurations; Papillary (~0.78) and Lepidic (~0.83) are the weak classes.
REASONING: Further tweaks to early fusion cannot plausibly clear the acceptance threshold. The one open structural question is whether the gated model's weakness comes from PCA 32, since in early fusion keeping full dimensions beat PCA 16/32. This trial runs gated with L2, no PCA, a small hidden layer (16), heavy dropout (0.5) and strong weight decay (1.0) for a short schedule (100 epochs). This is the most regularised gated setting, so it uses the full feature space while limiting overfitting on 134 patients per fold.
EXPECTED: Most likely AUROC around 0.875-0.885 with a larger fold SD, i.e. rejected. A clear gain over 0.885 would mean per-patient gating adds information once it sees full-dimensional features. If it fails, gated fusion is ruled out; I would spend the remaining trials on at most one late_tuned or stack check and then accept that early fusion (#8, about +0.015 over uni2h+meta) is the answer.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with per-slide L2 normalisation, no PCA and strong shrinkage (C=1e-4) plateaus at about 0.885 (#8, #10, #13, #20). These runs are about 0.015 above the best single model, uni2h+meta at 0.870. Changes to meta_weight, balance_blocks, L2 and PCA all move AUROC by less than 0.001. Late averaging of probabilities or logits, learned_weights and gated all sit 0.005-0.02 lower. Only late_tuned stack has been tried, at stack_C=0.01 (0.867), and it may have been over-shrunk.
REASONING: The early-fusion neighbourhood is exhausted, and the only C value below the current one does not exist in the grid. The main untested mechanism that could still beat simple averaging is a stacker with weaker regularisation. It can learn class-specific weights per model, for example letting different models lead on Papillary versus Lepidic, which are the weakest classes. stack_C=0.1 is a middle value: 0.01 likely collapsed toward a near-constant output, and 1.0 risks overfitting 21 log-probability inputs on about 107 inner-CV patients.
EXPECTED: If class-specific weighting helps, AUROC should reach about 0.89 or more, with gains in Papillary and Lepidic. If it lands at or below about 0.88, stacking adds no usable signal at this sample size. Early fusion with L2 and C=1e-4 would then stand as the final answer.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with heavy shrinkage (C=1e-4, no PCA, L2 or not, balanced or not) has plateaued at about 0.885. That is roughly +0.015 over the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Every variation of meta_weight, PCA, L2 and balance_blocks lands within noise of #8. Late, late_tuned, stack and gated variants are all worse; gated is noisier and lower.
REASONING: Only 3 trials remain before the stop rule. The one untested direction with any plausible upside is weighted_vote in late_tuned. Its neighbour mean_logit got 0.881, and weighted_vote may weight the stronger members differently. Two other options are low-value. C is already at its minimum of 1e-4 for early, so there is nothing further below. Raising C from 0.001 to 0.0001 already gave +0.003, so the trend points toward strong shrinkage, not weaker. weighted_vote at least answers an open question: it is the only untested combine rule.
EXPECTED: Likely about 0.875-0.882 and rejected, since vote-based combining loses probability resolution for AUROC. If rejected, I would conclude that heavily regularised early concatenation (#8) is the robust fusion choice. Its gain over the single-model baselines is about +0.015.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with per-slide L2, no PCA, strong shrinkage (C=1e-4) and balanced blocks (#8, 0.8852) is the best so far. It clearly beats the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.8701). Its neighbours (meta_weight, balance_blocks, L2, PCA 128, early_tuned) all fall within ±0.001, so this region is a flat plateau. Late, late_tuned and gated variants are consistently 0.005-0.02 lower, and stacking improved as stack_C rose (0.8672 at 0.01, 0.8732 at 0.1).
REASONING: Further early-fusion tweaks cannot clear the acceptance threshold, because the plateau is flat and C is already at the grid minimum. The one open question with a visible trend is stacking at the weakest stack regularisation (stack_C=1.0). Here the meta-learner can learn class-specific model weights, for example leaning on the model that is best for Papillary or Lepidic. That is the only remaining mechanism that could add something early fusion cannot.
EXPECTED: Most likely about 0.875-0.880, still below #8. If it does not beat #8 by more than the threshold, I conclude that the stacker has too few patients (134 per fold) to learn class-wise weights. In that case #8 (early, L2, C=1e-4, balanced blocks) stands as the final fusion, about +0.015 AUROC over the best single model.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion of L2-normalised full embeddings at strong regularisation (C=1e-4) has plateaued at about 0.885 AUROC. Trials #8, #9, #10, #13, #16 and #20 all fall within ±0.001 of each other. That is clearly above the best single model (uni2h+meta 0.870). Late, stacked, learned-weight and gated fusion are consistently worse, and gated and stack also show higher fold variance. Papillary (about 0.78) and Lepidic (about 0.83) remain the weak classes, and no knob has moved them.
REASONING: This is the last trial before the stop rule fires. The one remaining open question in the best-performing family is early_tuned with heavier metadata weight at C=1e-4. It combines per-block weights learned by inner CV with metadata weight 10, the setting tuned for H-optimus-1 alone, and it is the only untested early-family variant that changes the effective regularisation per block. Other untested options, such as PCA 64 or a different gated setting, are either bracketed by tested settings or high-variance with poor results so far.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.884-0.886, inside the noise threshold, so it will be rejected and the search will stop. If so, I conclude that the fusion gain (about +0.015 over the best single model) is saturated. Trial #8, plain early concatenation with L2 normalisation and strong shrinkage, is then the final choice, and finer fusion machinery adds nothing at n=167.
